module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil


/-!
# Partitions of $n$ into distinct non-squarefree parts for $n > 23$

a: Number of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts that are not squarefree.
This is the number of finite subsets of positive integers $P$ such that
$\sum_{k \in P} k = n$ and every element $k \in P$ is not squarefree.

*References:*
- [A256012](https://oeis.org/A256012)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA256012


open Nat Finset

/--
a: Number of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts that are not squarefree.
This is the number of finite subsets of positive integers $P$ such that
$\sum_{k \in P} k = n$ and every element $k \in P$ is not squarefree.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  -- The parts must be $\le n$ to sum to $n$.
  -- This is $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$
  let potential_parts : Finset ℕ := range (n + 1) \ {0}

  -- We count all subsets P of potential_parts that satisfy the sum and the property.
  card <| filter (fun P : Finset ℕ =>
    P.sum id = n ∧
    (∀ k ∈ P, ¬ Squarefree k)
  ) (powerset potential_parts)


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 0 := by decide +kernel

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 0 := by decide +kernel

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 0 := by decide +kernel

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 1 := by decide +kernel


/--
Conjecture: $a(n) > 0$ for $n > 23$.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/256012.wip.lean#L91"]
theorem a_pos_of_gt (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 23) : a n > 0 := by
    sorry

end OeisA256012

review.notes:
Checked all seven declarations. The definition counts exactly partitions into distinct positive nonsquarefree parts. Excluding zero is correct, and restricting parts to ≤ n loses no partition. The empty partition gives a(0)=1, matching OEIS. The theorem's strict threshold n>23 matches the source verbatim.

Lean experiments proved that a(n)>0 is equivalent to existence of the intended finite set of parts. Computed values through n=30 matched OEIS; kernel-checked examples also confirmed the source's values at n=20,…,25, including a(23)=0 and a(24)=4. All five existing test lemmas have only standard axioms.

OEIS records the conjecture as proved on May 26, 2026, consistent with `research solved`. The separate AlphaProof Nexus proof linked by OEIS compiled with the current import substituted; its counting definition is definitionally equal to this file's, and its theorem proves the exact statement without sorry or nonstandard axioms. The formal-conjectures GitHub/fork link was not consulted. The main OEIS website returned a Cloudflare challenge, so its complete entry was read from the official OEIS data mirror instead.
